stem: After interdisciplinary evaluation, the transplant team determines that a candidate does not meet selection criteria. What is the appropriate coordinator communication with the candidate?

options.text: Inform the patient that they do not meet selection criteria and will not be placed on the waiting list
List the patient immediately without discussing the team decision
Defer all communication until an organ offer is received
Refer the patient to the OPO to self-register on the national waiting list

explanation.rationale_correct: Evaluation outcome references include informing patients when they do not meet selection criteria and will not be placed on the waiting list, as part of communicating team recommendations.

rationale_incorrect.B: Candidates who do not meet selection criteria are not listed without team communication.
rationale_incorrect.C: Team recommendations must be communicated at evaluation conclusion, not deferred until organ offer.
rationale_incorrect.D: Waitlist registration occurs through the transplant program after selection, not independent OPO self-registration.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → §7. Selection criteria and evaluation outcome → c.iv.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: The patient does not meet selection criteria and will not be placed on the waiting list

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → §7. Selection criteria and evaluation outcome → c.iv. (not listed); PDF p. 101 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Distinct 020400 angle from cctc-2007 (MELD change education); anchor verified on Cupples p. 101.

stem: Before the selection committee meeting, which coordinator responsibility is described in standard interdisciplinary evaluation references?

options.text: Synthesize information from interdisciplinary team members and physical assessments for presentation at the selection committee meeting
Unilaterally approve or deny transplantation without team input
Perform the transplant operation when the surgeon is unavailable
Set OPTN allocation policy for the region

explanation.rationale_correct: The transplant coordinator synthesizes interdisciplinary evaluation information and physical assessment findings for presentation at the selection committee meeting.

rationale_incorrect.B: Selection decisions are interdisciplinary; coordinators synthesize information rather than unilaterally approving transplantation.
rationale_incorrect.C: Coordinators do not perform transplant surgery.
rationale_incorrect.D: OPTN allocation policy is set at the national policy level, not by individual coordinators.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → interdisciplinary team → iii. Transplant coordinator
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Synthesizes information from interdisciplinary team members and physical assessments for presentation at selection committee meeting

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → interdisciplinary team roles → iii. Transplant coordinator (selection committee presentation); PDF p. 96 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Distinct 020300 angle from cctc-2001/2003; anchor verified on Cupples p. 96.

stem: When registering a candidate on the OPTN waiting list, how must transplant programs report HLA typing information?

options.text: Using current World Health Organization (WHO) nomenclature
Using only informal center-specific abbreviations not reported to OPTN
HLA typing is optional and never submitted at registration
Using only donor-specific refusal codes instead of HLA data

explanation.rationale_correct: OPTN policy requires transplant programs to report HLA information using current WHO nomenclature when the candidate is registered on the waiting list.

rationale_incorrect.B: Listing documentation requires standardized WHO HLA nomenclature reported to OPTN, not informal abbreviations only.
rationale_incorrect.C: HLA reporting is required for waiting list registration per OPTN policy tables.
rationale_incorrect.D: Refusal codes document declined offers; they do not replace HLA registration requirements.

primary_anchor.section: Policy 3.4 → Waiting List Registration (HLA reporting table before 3.4.E)
primary_anchor.quote_hint: report this HLA information using current World Health Organization (WHO) nomenclature when the candidate is registered

references.locator: Policy 3.4 → Waiting List Registration (HLA reporting using WHO nomenclature); PDF p. 44 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. OPTN-primary anchor verified on indexed optn_policies.pdf p. 44.

stem: A lung transplant candidate with a recent smoking history is being considered for listing. Which pre-transplant requirement aligns with standard pulmonary evaluation references?

options.text: A period of smoking cessation confirmed by random urine cotinine testing
Immediate listing without pulmonary function testing
Waiving oxygen saturation assessment for all smokers
Permanent exclusion from transplantation after any lifetime smoking exposure

explanation.rationale_correct: Most lung transplant programs require a period of smoking cessation before listing patients who currently smoke or have recent smoking history, with cessation confirmed by random urine cotinine testing.

rationale_incorrect.B: Smoking history warrants pulmonary function testing and smoking-cessation requirements before listing.
rationale_incorrect.C: All referred candidates should have pulse oximetry; smoking history adds further requirements.
rationale_incorrect.D: Recent smoking requires cessation and confirmation, not automatic permanent exclusion for all prior exposure.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 1, Pretransplant Evaluation → §2. Pulmonary evaluation → d.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: period of smoking cessation before listing patients who are currently smoking … Smoking cessation is confirmed by random urine cotinine testing

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 1 → §2. Pulmonary evaluation → d. (smoking cessation and cotinine testing before listing); PDF p. 33 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Second lung organ item; anchor verified on Cupples p. 33.
